title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, Top Issues & Canonical Fixes
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Canonical playbook for producing and operating Developer Experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues with canonical fixes.
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines the standards, templates and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and a curated list of top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is fast, consistent onboarding for engineers and customers and reproducible fixes for frequently-reported problems.

Scope:
- All public-facing SDK guides and quickstarts (Python, TypeScript, Go).
- API example snippets used in docs and SDK reference pages.
- Docs site operations (deploy, review, rollback, analytics).
- Triage and canonical fixes for top support issues reported by Customer Success and Support.

Audience:
- Developer docs owners, SDK engineers, solutions engineers, technical writers, and support engineers.

Principles:
- Single source of truth: keep canonical examples in the docs repo and sync to SDK repos.
- Reproducibility: examples must be runnable with minimal configuration and deterministic outputs where feasible.
- Observability-first: docs include cost/latency expectations and how to measure them.
- Fast remediation: known issues must have verified, copy-paste fixes and test cases.

1) Documentation structure and templates

A. High-level page layout (recommended):
- Title + short 1-2 sentence intro
- When to use this guide (audience/assumptions)
- Prerequisites (accounts, API keys, SDK versions)
- Step-by-step quickstart (copy-paste runnable)
- API example gallery (concise snippets)
- Troubleshooting / top issues (links to canonical fixes)
- Operational notes (performance, cost, SLOs)
- Further reading / related pages

B. Quickstart template (required fields):
1. Prerequisites
   - CLI or SDK version (exact semantic versions)
   - Environment variables: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION
2. Install
   - Install command(s) (pip/npm/go get)
3. Minimal runnable example (20-40 lines)
4. Expected output and validation steps
5. Next steps and links to advanced guides

C. SDK guide template
- Overview + compatibility matrix
- Authentication examples (short, secure patterns)
- Core flows: generation, streaming, function/tool calling, embeddings, reranking
- Error handling patterns and retries (idempotency keys, status codes to treat as retryable)
- Performance tuning knobs (batching, cache headers, request hints)
- End-to-end sample app reference with link to GitHub template

2) Canonical API examples

- Store canonical snippets in /repos/docs/canonical-examples as single-file runnable examples. Each snippet must include a header with the supported SDK version, API surface (text/gen, chat, embeddings), and a one-line cost/latency expectation.

Example header (text):

# SDK: python@0.9.1 | API: chat.generate | Expected latency: 60-150ms per token (hosted)

Rules for examples:
- Avoid secrets in code; use environment variables.
- Provide both sync and streaming variants where applicable.
- Include minimal test harness (unit test or smoke test) that runs in CI.
- Mark platform-specific examples (hosted vs dedicated vs private) in the header.

3) Docs-site operating procedures

A. Ownership and cadence:
- Docs on-call: rotated weekly from Developer Experience team. Pager duty: devexp-docs-oncall@squad.redwood (link internal).
- Content reviews: any PR touching stable guides requires 1 technical reviewer + 1 technical writer.
- Monthly audit: identify > 6-month-old quickstarts and verify they still run.

B. Deployment checklist (pre-deploy):
1. CI green (lint + linkcheck + smoke examples)
2. Spellcheck and accessibility scan passed
3. Versioned SDK examples updated if relevant
4. Cross-links validated (no broken internal links)
5. Stakeholder review completed for breaking changes

C. Deployment procedure (production docs site):
1. Create release branch: docs/release/YYYY-MM-DD-<short>
2. Merge PRs into branch and run full CI (including smoke examples against the staging API key)
3. Run QA smoke: run 5 representative quickstarts and validate outputs
4. Promote to staging site and run linkcheck + analytics smoke
5. If OK, merge branch into main and trigger production deploy via CI (auto invalidates CDN cache)
6. Post-deploy: check error budget (docs pages 500/404), and monitor Redwood Docs analytics for traffic anomalies for 48 hours

D. Rollback:
- If critical regressions occur (broken quickstarts, large number of link failures, or CI errors), revert the production deploy commit and re-deploy previous tag. Follow the incident process and notify stakeholders.

4) Top support issues and canonical fixes (2026 Q1 snapshot)

This section lists the top recurring support issues experienced by customer success and the canonical fixes maintained in the docs repo. Each entry includes: Issue summary, Symptoms, Root cause, Canonical fix (copy-paste), Verification steps, and Owner.

Example issues:

1) Auth failures - 401 on hosted API requests
- Symptoms: SDK calls return HTTP 401 immediately
- Root cause: expired/misconfigured REDWOOD_API_KEY or using staging key against production endpoint
- Canonical fix:
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-key>"
   export REDWOOD_REGION="us-west-2"
   # For Python SDK ensure: pip install redwood-sdk==<supported-version>
- Verification: run `python examples/chat_smoke.py` and expect 200 OK and a non-empty content payload
- Owner: solutions-eng@redwood

2) Streaming hangs for long responses
- Symptoms: client receives partial stream then stalls after ~10-20s
- Root cause: network proxies or keepalive timeouts dropping connections; incorrect usage of streaming iterator in client code
- Canonical fix:
   - Ensure SDK version >= 0.9.0 (contains streaming keepalive fixes)
   - If behind corporate proxy, set HTTP_KEEPALIVE=60 and configure proxy keepalive accordingly
   - Client pattern (Python):
     for chunk in client.chat.stream(...):
         process(chunk)
       # avoid re-wrapping stream in another async loop
- Verification: run streaming smoke and assert continuous token flow for a 120-token prompt
- Owner: eng-developer-experience

3) High tail latency for small prompt workloads
- Symptoms: P95/P99 latency spikes on low QPS endpoints
- Root cause: Client-side batching disabled + cold-worker scheduling on Dedicated pools
- Canonical fix:
   - Enable client batching hints: X-Redwood-Batch-Window=20ms
   - For Dedicated: configure autoscale-min=2 for pools serving low-QPS customers
- Verification: run load test (wrk or k6) with 1rps sustained and verify P99 falls within SLA baseline
- Owner: eng-sre / eng-serving-runtime

4) Mismatched token accounting between docs examples and billing
- Symptoms: Developers see different token counts than docs show in examples
- Root cause: Example uses older model variant (different tokenizer) or includes trailing whitespace in prompts
- Canonical fix:
   - Update canonical example header to include model_id and tokenizer version
   - Trim inputs in examples: prompt = prompt.strip()
- Verification: run tokenizer count script included in repo and assert token count matches billing estimate
- Owner: finance-and-legal + eng-developer-experience

5) Change control and release notes

- Every docs release must include a CHANGELOG entry with: changed pages, SDK version bumps, canonical example updates, and migration notes. Use conventional commit format for doc PRs: docs(scope): short summary

6) Template checklist for new quickstarts

- [ ] Title and 1-line description
- [ ] Audience and assumptions
- [ ] Exact SDK versions + install commands
- [ ] Minimal runnable example (passes smoke test)
- [ ] Expected output and validation steps
- [ ] Troubleshooting section with at least 2 likely issues and fixes
- [ ] Links to sample app repo and advanced guides
- [ ] Labels: sdk, quickstart, stable/experimental, audience (dev/platform)

7) Metrics & KPIs for DevEx docs health

- CI smoke pass rate (target: 99% per release)
- Quickstart run-to-success rate in staging (target: 95%)
- Time to merge doc PRs (target: median 2 business days)
- Top support issue re-open rate (target: <5%)

8) Ownership, contacts, and escalation

- DevEx Docs Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-developer-experience)
- Docs on-call rotation: see internal schedule (devexp-docs-oncall)
- Support escalation: for pager-triggering regressions open an incident and page eng-sre and product oncall

9) Appendix: common CLI commands and CI helpers

- Run local site: make docs-serve
- Run smoke examples: scripts/run_smoke_examples.sh --staging-key=${REDWOOD_API_KEY_STAGING}
- Update canonical examples: tools/update_examples.py --sdk python --version 0.9.1
